identity_evidence: Text: Executive Order 273, signed November 15, 1904, Isthmian Canal Commission positions added to Schedule A
outliers_found: amends the general civil-service rules (Schedule A) rather than governing the Zone
civil-service schedule operates through the U.S. Civil Service Commission beyond the Zone
basis: The order amends Schedule A of the civil-service rules to except listed Isthmian Canal Commission positions from examination. That is an amendment to the general civil-service rules, which the lot card lists as an outlier, so it is not upheld for this lot.
operative_quote: Schedule A of the civil-service rules is hereby amended by adding at the end thereof a new section, reading:
notes: Page header says it was superseded by EO 394 (1906); that is outside the order's own text and was not relied on.

identity_evidence: Text: Executive Order 3213, signed January 9, 1920, costs and security for costs in the District Court and Magistrates' Courts in the Panama Canal Zone
basis: The order prescribes court rules (docket fees, jury fee, security for costs) for the Canal Zone District Court and Magistrates' Courts only. Those courts and the Zone ended with the 1979 treaty regime, with U.S. court jurisdiction ending about 1982.
end_or_bound: no later than 1982-03-31 (Zone courts' transitional jurisdiction ended)
operative_quote: I hereby establish and prescribe the following rules of practice to govern the District Court and the Magistrates' Courts in the Panama Canal Zone:

identity_evidence: Heading 'Healing Arts Practice Regulations for the Canal Zone'; GPO 1933 imprint; the order number and day-month date are not legible in the available text
basis: Everything visible regulates licensing of healing-art practice in the Canal Zone through the Zone Board of Health, which would fit the lot. The text file is truncated (original 26,314 characters, cut at Section 15), so the remaining sections and any other clause cannot be read, and the order is not upheld.
operative_quote:
I hereby prescribe the following regulations governing the issue of licenses to practice
the healing art in the Canal Zone.
notes: Truncated at Section 15 (marker '[TRUNCATED: original 26314 characters]'). Identity rests on title and 1933 only; number 6219 and date 1933-07-26 do not appear in the text. Section 13 gives licensing without examination to former canal physicians; the remainder is unseen. Likely upholdable if the full text shows nothing of another kind.

outliers_found: not a Canal Zone order: concerns free transportation on the Government railway in Alaska
basis: The order gives free transportation to Government employees on the Alaska railroad under the 1914 Alaska railroad act. It has nothing to do with the Canal Zone and does not belong to the lot.
operative_quote:
it is hereby ordered
that free transportation shall be furnished employees of the United States
Government when their official duties require them to travel over the lines
of the Government railway in Alaska,
notes: Item is misfiled in lot L5.

identity_evidence: Text: Executive Order 3032, signed January 25, 1919, revoking the April 9, 1917 order placing the canal and Zone under Army control
basis: The order terminates an earlier order that had put the Panama Canal and the Canal Zone government under Army command. Its only command is that revocation, which was carried out on issue, and the Zone government it concerned ceased in 1979.
end_or_bound: no later than 1979-10-01 (Zone government ended); command spent on issue 1919-01-25
operative_quote: officer of the Army commanding the United States' troops stationed in the Canal Zone, is hereby terminated and shall be no longer in force.
notes: The command is a one-time revocation, so it is arguably spent on issue; a later date of 1999-12-31 would also be safe.

identity_evidence: Text: renames Culebra Cut as Gaillard Cut; dated April 27, 1915, signed Woodrow Wilson
outliers_found: honorific naming of a canal feature, not governance, regulation, fees, lands or employment conditions
name continues in use, so the command is not clearly spent
basis: The order renames a section of the canal in honor of Lieutenant-Colonel Gaillard. It does not govern the Zone or the canal's operation in any of the ways the lot describes, and a name given by order may still be used, so a NO status is not supported on this text.
operative_quote: It is hereby ordered that the portion of the Panama Canal through the continental divide heretofore known as "Culebra Cut" shall hereafter be named "Gaillard Cut"
notes: Number 2185 does not appear in the text; identity rests on date, signer and subject.

identity_evidence: Text: Executive Order 1353, 'To Provide for the Collection of a Distillation Tax', Taft, 'order for the Canal Zone'
basis: The order sets a distillation tax, licensing, bonds and criminal penalties for distilleries in the Canal Zone, collected by the Zone's Collector of Revenues. It applies only within the Zone and ended with Zone government.
end_or_bound: no later than 1979-10-01 (Zone government ended); penalty enforcement through Zone courts no later than 1982-03-31
operative_quote:
there shall 
be collected the sum of ten cents on each and every litre or fraction thereof
notes: Date conflict: page header says signed May 13, 1911 (matches the claim) but the signature block reads 'The White House, May 11, 1911'. Number and subject agree.

identity_evidence: Text: Executive Order 370, signed November 15, 1905, appointments in the Isthmian Canal service without examination
outliers_found: civil-service appointment rule that runs through the U.S. Civil Service Commission
refers to the 'Isthmus of Panama', not defined as the Canal Zone
not a Zone-government, regulation or fee order
basis: The order lets the Civil Service Commission allow temporary appointments, later made permanent, when no eligible is on a register for Isthmian Canal Commission service. It is a civil-service appointment rule operating through a general U.S. body, so it is uncertain that it fits the lot, and under the strict standard it is not upheld.
operative_quote: the Civil Service Commission may allow a temporary appointment, which may be made permanent on certificate
notes: Page header says revoked by EO 393 (January 12, 1906), which would support an earlier end, but that note is outside the order's own text. Reasonable to review individually.

identity_evidence: Text: Executive Order 2135, signed Woodrow Wilson February 4, 1915, accounting to the Treasury for Panama Canal collections
basis: The order prescribes how the Collector of the Panama Canal accounts for tolls, rentals and other canal receipts, including semi-annual audits in the Zone. It applies only to the U.S. operation of the canal, which ended on December 31, 1999.
end_or_bound: no later than 1999-12-31 (U.S. canal operation ended)
operative_quote: I hereby prescribe the following regulations governing accounting to the Treasury of the United States for moneys received on account of the Panama Canal by the collecting officers:
notes: Accounting runs through the War Department Auditor and Treasury Comptroller, but only for canal receipts; the order expressly excludes Zone Government revenues from the accounts.

identity_evidence: Text: Executive Order 928, August 14, 1908, amends Section 344 of the Penal Code of the Canal Zone
basis: The order amends the Canal Zone Penal Code so that grand larceny carries up to ten years' imprisonment. The Zone code applied only in the Zone, and Zone government and courts ended by 1979 and 1982.
end_or_bound: no later than 1982-03-31 (Zone penal law enforced through Zone courts)
operative_quote:
Section 344 of the Penal Code of the Canal Zone is amended to read as follows:

"Section 344. Grand larceny is punishable by imprisonment in the penitentiary not exceeding ten years."

identity_evidence: Text dated 'Septemier 8, 1909' [sic], signed Wm. H. Taft, amending Section 454 of Act No. 14 of the Laws of the Canal Zone on night hunting and spring guns
basis: The order rewrites a Canal Zone hunting law, with permits issued by the Zone Treasurer and a misdemeanor penalty for night hunting. It applies only in the Zone, which no longer exists.
end_or_bound: no later than 1982-03-31 (Zone law enforced through Zone courts)
operative_quote:
Section 454 of Act No. 14 of the Laws of the Canal Zone is amended
to read as follows:
notes: The order number 1126 does not appear in the text; identity rests on date, signer and subject, which agree with the claimed title. OCR typo 'Septemier'.

identity_evidence: Text: Executive Order 3031, January 25, 1919, 'Executive Order for the Canal Zone', leave credit for employees returning from military service
outliers_found: covers Panama Railroad Company employees, whose service was not limited to the Zone and rests partly on corporate arrangements
leave credit for former service members is a conditions-of-service right that may belong to general rules
basis: The order credits leave to employees of The Panama Canal or the Panama Railroad Company who return from war service. The Railroad Company's operations and employees extended beyond the Zone, which is an outlier under the lot card, so the order is not upheld.
operative_quote: shall, upon return to duty with The Panama Canal or Panama Railroad Company within the periods designated, be credited with leave
notes: Reasonable to review individually; the Zone label in the text may be enough for an individual reviewer.

identity_evidence: Text: '[No. 4801]', Calvin Coolidge, February 2, 1928, relating to licensing bicycles in the Canal Zone
basis: The order revokes the bicycle license and tag requirements and fees in the Canal Zone effective July 1, 1928, and leaves other bicycle rules in force. It is a Zone regulation that ended with Zone government.
operative_quote:
prescribing that privately-owned bicycles operated in the Canal
Z~u shall be licensed and carry license tags, and prescribing fees therefor,
are hereby revoked, effective on and after July 1, 1928.
notes: OCR damage ('Z~u', garbled number line); the sentence leaving other bicycle regulations in force is a savings clause, not a separate command.

identity_evidence: Text: Executive Order 1409, Taft, September 8, 1911, establishing the postal savings system in the Canal Zone
basis: The order creates a Zone postal savings system with a Board of Trustees drawn from Zone officers, set deposit rules and sets court-judgment recognition. The system and its government ended with the Zone; depositors' claims to funds were accrued effects of the order.
operative_quote: There is hereby established in the post offices of the Canal Zone a postal savings system, to be operated without the payment of interest on the deposits
notes: Claimed date was year-only ('1911'); the text gives September 8, 1911. Individual depositor claims are not a rights-creating clause of the order itself.

identity_evidence: Text: '[No. 4971]', Calvin Coolidge, September 28, 1928, designating the Secretary of State on commercial aircraft between the Canal Zone and foreign countries
basis: The order uses the President's Panama Canal Act power to name the Secretary of State to receive and decide applications to fly commercial aircraft between the Zone and foreign countries. That permission power concerned operation from the Zone and ended with U.S. administration of it.
end_or_bound: no later than 1999-12-31 (Zone and canal operation ended; Zone government ended 1979-10-01)
operative_quote:
I designate the Secretary of State
to receive and pass upon all applications for the privilege of operating commercial
fir' ft between the Canal Zone and foreign countries,
notes: OCR damage ('fir' ft' for aircraft). The foreign-country end of the flights is a mild reach beyond the Zone; I treated it as incidental to a Zone permission.

identity_evidence: Text: Executive Order 1755, Woodrow Wilson, March 24, 1913, suspending the February 26, 1913 order on claims for injuries to canal and Panama Railroad employees
outliers_found: continues compensation under general federal compensation acts and a statute, a continuing individual right
order operates by suspending another order until further notice
basis: The order suspends an earlier compensation order and continues payments for injury or death of Isthmian Canal Commission and Panama Railroad Company employees under federal acts of 1908, 1909 and 1911 and Zone laws. It reaches the Railroad Company and compensation rights under general U.S. statutes, which are outliers under the lot card.
operative_quote: It is ordered, That the operation of the said Order of February 26, 1913, is hereby suspended until further executive order or direction in the premises;
